verdict.rationale: Rippling's own marketing documents user-defined rules and custom workflows that run without manual intervention: dynamic access rules, offboarding-triggered retrieval flows, security-threat notification workflows, and "You define the rules, Rippling runs the rest." These are event-triggered background automations. Evidence on how users author and configure them is thin, all of it is vendor claims, and nothing shows recurring or scheduled runs, so coverage is partial. missing for 10: documentation of the workflow builder (triggers, conditions, actions setup), evidence of scheduled/recurring background runs (only event-triggered automations are shown), monitoring/logging of autonomous runs, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can set up automations that run autonomously in the background

citations.quote: You define the rules, Rippling runs the rest.
dynamic rules automatically ensure the right people get the right level of access—even as their roles change.
Custom workflows will automatically notify you of any security threats—no manual device checks or data pulls required.
The instant an employee is offboarded in Rippling, AI triggers the retrieval flow and generates the shipping label, dispatches the box, and tracks the return.
